reason: Conversation 2 correctly identified dE as a door-not-closed/locked error from the first turn, asked the right question (anything caught in the seal), and once the customer reported the duvet bulging and a corner squashed in the seal it gave the correct diagnosis: obstruction preventing the latch from engaging, no fault. Conversation 1 misread dE as a door-won't-open/child-lock issue, pushed an unnecessary power reset, then wrongly attributed the error to an 'unbalanced load' even after the customer described the duvet jammed in the seal, and closed by telling the customer the dE code was caused by load clumping - a diagnosis that is simply incorrect. Conversation 2's final advice about how to actually wash the duvet was partly speculative (balance-related framing, towel padding) and it did not clearly say the king-size duvet may simply be too big for this machine, but it did warn not to force the load and to use a bulky/duvet programme, which is reasonable; neither conversation recommended an unjustified part.
